title: SQL injection in Play Slick query
description: A Play controller builds a Slick filter by string concatenation with request input.
patch:
--- a/UserController.scala
+++ b/UserController.scala
@@ -2,4 +2,6 @@
-  val q = sql"select * from users where name like '%#$term%'".as[User]
+  val q = sql"select * from users where name like \$like".on(
+    "like" -> s"%${term}%")
root_cause: User input is interpolated into the SQL string rather than bound as a parameter.
attack: term=%' UNION SELECT card,cvv FROM cards -- exfiltrates data.
fix: Use Slick's parameter binding (.on(...)) for all dynamic values.
guideline: Bind parameters in Slick; never interpolate into SQL strings.

title: Container running as root with privileged
description: A Kubernetes Pod manifest runs as root with privileged: true, enabling host escape.
vulnerable_code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: app:1.0
    securityContext:
      privileged: true   # Vulnerable
      runAsUser: 0       # Vulnerable: root
secure_code:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: app:1.0
    securityContext:
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
patch:
--- a/pod.yaml
+++ b/pod.yaml
@@ -3,7 +3,14 @@
-    securityContext:
-      privileged: true
-      runAsUser: 0
+  securityContext:
+    runAsNonRoot: true
+    runAsUser: 1000
+    seccompProfile:
+      type: RuntimeDefault
+    securityContext:
+      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
+      capabilities: { drop: ["ALL"] }
root_cause: Privileged root containers can escape to the node via the kernel.
attack: A compromised container mounts /host and reads node secrets or pivots.
fix: Run as non-root, drop capabilities, disable privilege escalation, use seccomp.
guideline: Apply Pod Security Standards; never run privileged/root in prod.

title: MCP tool exposes destructive operation without auth
description: A Model Context Protocol tool registers a delete-everything function without auth/confirmation scoping.
secure_code:
# MCP server tool
@mcp.tool()
def delete_records(tenant_id: str, ids: list[str], ctx: AuthCtx) -> str:
    # Secure: scoped to caller tenant, list-based, audited, requires permission
    if not ctx.has_permission('record:delete'):
        raise PermissionError('forbidden')
    db.execute(
        "DELETE FROM records WHERE tenant_id=:t AND id = ANY(:ids)",
        {'t': tenant_id, 'ids': ids})
    audit.log(ctx.user, 'delete_records', len(ids))
    return f"deleted {len(ids)}"
patch:
--- a/mcp_tools.py
+++ b/mcp_tools.py
@@ -2,5 +2,11 @@
-def delete_all_records() -> str:
-    db.execute("DELETE FROM records")
+def delete_records(tenant_id: str, ids: list[str], ctx: AuthCtx) -> str:
+    if not ctx.has_permission('record:delete'): raise PermissionError('forbidden')
+    db.execute("DELETE FROM records WHERE tenant_id=:t AND id = ANY(:ids)", {'t':tenant_id,'ids':ids})
+    audit.log(ctx.user, 'delete_records', len(ids))
root_cause: An agent-facing tool performs broad destructive actions with no authorization or scoping.
attack: An LLM agent (or prompt-injected request) calls delete_all_records() to wipe tenant data.
impact: Mass data loss due to excessive agency granted to the model/tool.
fix: Scope tools per tenant, require explicit permissions, prefer list-based actions, and audit them.
guideline: Least-privilege MCP tools: scope, authorize, prefer explicit over bulk, and audit.

title: WebView loads arbitrary URL with JS enabled
description: An Android WebView enables JavaScript and loads any intent-supplied URL, enabling bridge abuse.
vulnerable_code:
val web = findViewById<WebView>(R.id.web)
// Vulnerable: JS on, file access on, untrusted URL
web.settings.javaScriptEnabled = true
web.settings.allowFileAccess = true
web.loadUrl(intent.getStringExtra("url")!!)
secure_code:
val web = findViewById<WebView>(R.id.web)
// Secure: disable JS unless required, block file access, validate host
web.settings.javaScriptEnabled = false
web.settings.allowFileAccess = false
web.settings.allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs = false
val url = intent.getStringExtra("url") ?: return
if (URL(url).host != "trusted.example.com") return
web.loadUrl(url)
patch:
--- a/MainActivity.kt
+++ b/MainActivity.kt
@@ -2,5 +2,9 @@
-web.settings.javaScriptEnabled = true
-web.settings.allowFileAccess = true
+web.settings.javaScriptEnabled = false
+web.settings.allowFileAccess = false
+web.settings.allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs = false
+if (URL(url).host != "trusted.example.com") return
root_cause: WebView is over-permissioned (JS + file access) and loads unvalidated URLs from intents.
attack: Malicious app or link drives the WebView to a file:// or javascript: URL to steal local data.
impact: Local file theft or JavaScript bridge abuse on the device.
fix: Disable JS/file access unless needed, validate hosts, and avoid loading intent URLs directly.
guideline: Minimize WebView permissions; validate hosts; prefer Chrome Custom Tabs.

description: A comment stored in the DB is rendered into the DOM via innerHTML without sanitization.
mitre_attack: T1059.007 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
patch:
--- a/routes.js +++ b/routes.js @@ -1,6 +1,8 @@ +const escapeHtml = s => s.replace(/[&<>\"]/g, ch => ({'&':'&','<':'<','>':'>','"':'"'}[ch])); - '
' + c.text + '
' + '
' + escapeHtml(c.text) + '
'
root_cause: Stored user content is emitted as raw HTML, executing attacker scripts in victims' browsers.
attack: Attacker posts a comment with that runs for every viewer.
impact: Session theft, worm-like propagation, account takeover.
fix: HTML-escape stored data on render, or use a sanitizer (DOMPurify) and safe DOM APIs (textContent).
guideline: Escape on output and prefer textContent / framework bindings over innerHTML.

title: IDOR on document download
description: A Rails controller loads a document purely by id without ownership check.
vulnerable_code:
def show
  # Vulnerable: no tenant/owner scope
  @doc = Document.find(params[:id])
end
secure_code:
def show
  # Secure: scope to current user
  @doc = current_user.documents.find(params[:id])
rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
  head :not_found
end
patch:
--- a/app/controllers/documents_controller.rb
+++ b/app/controllers/documents_controller.rb
@@ -1,4 +1,6 @@
-  @doc = Document.find(params[:id])
+  @doc = current_user.documents.find(params[:id])
+rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
+  head :not_found
root_cause: Object lookup is keyed only by attacker-controllable id, not by ownership.
attack: User changes id to access other tenants' documents.
fix: Scope queries to the authenticated principal/tenant.
guideline: Enforce object-level authorization; scope every lookup by owner/tenant.

title: Missing authorization on admin route
description: An Akka HTTP admin route has no authentication/authorization directive.
root_cause: The route enforces no authorization, so any caller can flush the cache.
attack: Attacker posts to /admin/flush to cause denial of service.
fix: Apply authentication and role-based authorization directives.
guideline: Protect admin routes with auth + role checks.
